So here we have a fallen angel. I'm naturally inclined to suggest a link to one of the other abrhamic SCP articles. One that comes to mind is the Tower of Babel skip that is found in SCP-1643, especially after the line "Subjects exposed to SCP-861 will allege that they understand fragments of the lyrics, but will deny any familiarity with the language." As such, I am proposing the following edits:

Changing this:

Subjects exposed to SCP-861 will allege that they understand fragments of the lyrics, but will deny any familiarity with the language. The quantity of song material understood, as well as its placement within the overall composition, vary widely from subject to subject. A compilation of ███ tests indicated a possible correlation between subjects with prominent humility and song comprehension. These subjects demonstrated a comprehension percentage as high as 89%, allowing for ██.██% of the song to be translated (see DOCUMENT-TRANSEPT-861 for details).

To this:

Subjects exposed to SCP-861 will allege that they understand fragments of the lyrics, but will deny any familiarity with the language. The quantity of song material understood, as well as its placement within the overall composition, vary widely from subject to subject. A compilation of ███ tests indicated a possible correlation between subjects with prominent humility and song comprehension. These subjects demonstrated a comprehension percentage as high as 89%, allowing for ██.██% of the song to be translated (see DOCUMENT-TRANSEPT-861 for details).

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

None of this makes sense to me on a psychological level. I don't see how you could "measure" arrogance and/or modesty. item.content:encoded: Also, Evangelion itself borrowed heavily from Judeochristian mythology. Given that this SCP is an interpretation of an angel as they're actually described in the Bible rather than the "regular people with wings and a halo" that popular culture has turned them into, it's not surprising that there's a lot of similarity. It would be like criticizing a cobbled-together golem for being a Frankenstein ripoff, rather than recognizing that they're both drawing off the Judaic golem myth/legend.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I might be jumping to conclusions a bit but… To me this seems like a Neon Genesis Evangelion expy for the following reasons:
SCP originates from a "class 2 impact" = the Second Impact.
"seven organs tentatively identified as eyes" = the 7-eyed Lilith.
Jewish mysticism galore!

Furthermore, the tone in which the SCP is written is not up to standard in my opinion. Overuse of "##-class" ("11-class munitions", etc.) as well as unscientific phrases such as "a melodious voice" and that bit about extra-dimensional beings doesn't fit with the cold, clinical, analytical tone of an SCP page.

And the worst offense, in my eyes, is that this SCP is just plain bland. There is nothing new or clever or interesting or frightening about it. There's no "hook". There's nothing that lingers in the mind of the reader, nothing to set it apart from "generic pseudo-kabalistic doomsday". The other points I raised may be forgivable, this one isn't.
